gold.label: Together: the gold move

steps.say: Gold works backwards. £96 is the price AFTER a 20% increase, so it equals the original times the multiplier. Find that multiplier.
steps.hint: An increase adds the rate to 1.

steps.say: The final price is original × 1.2. To get back to the original, divide instead of multiply.
steps.hint: Divide the final price by the multiplier.

steps.say: Check by going forwards: the original plus 20% should return £96.
steps.done: It lands back on £96, so the original was £80. Dividing by the multiplier is the gold move.

steps.say: One trap to avoid: taking 20% off the £96 gives a different, wrong number. See it.
steps.done: £96 − £19.20 = £76.80, which is NOT the original. Always divide by the multiplier instead.

gold.display: After a 20% increase, a coat costs £96. Find the original price.

steps.say: Bronze is one percentage change, done with a multiplier. This is an increase of 30%, so add 0.30 to 1.
steps.hint: Add the rate as a decimal to 1.

steps.say: Now multiply the original amount by it.
Read the answer back to be sure.
steps.hint: Subtract the original from the new price.

steps.say: And that increase should be 30% of 60.
steps.done: 18 matches, so £78 is right. That is the whole bronze move.

steps.say: Silver adds compounding: the same percentage applied several times. First the yearly multiplier for a 5% increase.
steps.hint: Add the rate as a decimal to 1.

steps.say: It runs for 3 years, so raise the multiplier to the power 3.
Multiply the starting amount by this single factor.
Check the interest earned looks right for 3 years.
steps.done: £630.50 interest on £4000 over 3 years at 5% compound. The power did the work: that is the silver move.

steps.say: No formulas yet. A £40 hoodie has 25% off. 25% of £40 is a quarter, which is £10.
That is the whole idea. Taking 25% off is the same as keeping 75%, and 75% as a decimal is 0.75, so \(£40 \times 0.75 = £30\) in one step. That 0.75 is called the multiplier.
Now the twist. At the till you get a loyalty 10% off the £30 as well. 10% of £30 is £3.

Two cuts did NOT make 35% off (that would be £26). Each cut comes off a smaller price, so they stack up: \(£40 \times 0.75 \times 0.90 = £27\). Multiplying multipliers together is all compound change is.

steps: Identify the percentage and convert to a decimal multiplier
For compound change: raise the multiplier to the power of n (number of periods)
Multiply the original amount by the multiplier
method_card.title: How to Work with Percentages & Compound Change
method_card.content:
To find a percentage of an amount, convert the percentage to a decimal and multiply. For example, 15% of £200 = 0.15 × 200 = £30.

For a percentage increase or decrease, use a multiplier. Increase by 20% → multiply by 1.2. Decrease by 15% → multiply by 0.85.

Compound change applies the multiplier repeatedly: \(\text{Amount} \times \text{multiplier}^n\) where \(n\) is the number of time periods.

To find the original amount after a percentage change (reverse percentage), divide by the multiplier.
method_card.example:
£5000 is invested at 3% compound interest for 4 years. Find the final amount.

Step 1: Multiplier = 1.03

Step 2: \(5000 \times 1.03^4 = 5000 \times 1.12550881 = \pounds5627.54\)

steps: You are given the amount AFTER a change and must work backwards. The final amount is original × multiplier, so divide by the multiplier to undo it.
For compound change, divide by \((\text{multiplier})^n\), or step back one year at a time. Never just take the percentage off the final amount: it applied to the original.
gold.title: Gold: reverse percentages and hidden rates

example.question: After a 25% increase, a coat costs £75. Find the original price.

steps: A single increase or decrease. Turn the percentage into a multiplier: an increase of \(r\%\) is \(1 + \frac{r}{100}\), a decrease is \(1 - \frac{r}{100}\).
Multiply the original amount by the multiplier. A 25% rise uses 1.25, a 20% fall uses 0.80. To find a percentage OF an amount, just multiply by the decimal.
Check by finding the change on its own: it should equal that percentage of the original.
bronze.title: Bronze: one percentage change

steps: Compound change applies the same percentage again and again. Find the yearly multiplier once, then raise it to the power of the number of years: \(\text{Final} = \text{Original} \times (\text{multiplier})^n\).
Simple interest is different: it adds the same amount every year, so find one year's interest and multiply by the number of years.
To write one amount as a percentage of another, divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100.
silver.title: Silver: compound change and percentage change

gold.display: After a 25% increase, a price is \(\pounds 60\). What was the original price?

misconceptions.message: £45 takes 25% off £60. The £60 is already after the rise, so divide: 60 ÷ 1.25 = £48.
£75 multiplies 60 × 1.25. To undo an increase, divide: 60 ÷ 1.25 = £48.
£80 divides by 0.75. A 25% increase uses 1.25: 60 ÷ 1.25 = £48.

gold.display: After a 30% reduction, a sofa costs \(\pounds 350\). What was the original price?

misconceptions.message: £455 adds 30% to £350. To undo a reduction, divide by 0.70: 350 ÷ 0.70 = £500.
£1166.67 divides by 0.30. A 30% reduction leaves 0.70: 350 ÷ 0.70 = £500.
£245 takes another 30% off. The £350 is already reduced, so divide: £500.

gold.hint: Multiply by 1.06 year by year until you pass £2500.
gold.display: \(\pounds 2000\) is invested at 6% compound interest. After how many years does it exceed \(\pounds 2500\)?

misconceptions.message: After 3 years it is £2382.03, still under £2500. Year 4 reaches £2524.95, so 4 years.
After 2 years it is £2247.20, well under £2500. It first passes £2500 after 4 years.

gold.hint: Two years AGO: divide by 1.05 squared.
gold.display: A painting increases in value by 5% each year. It is now worth \(\pounds 12\,000\). What was it worth 2 years ago?

misconceptions.message: £13 230 goes forward in time (12000 × 1.05²). Two years ago means divide: 12000 ÷ 1.05² = £10 884.35.
£11 400 only takes 5% off once. Divide by 1.05 twice: 12000 ÷ 1.05² = £10 884.35.

gold.display: A town's population decreases by 3% each year from 80 000. What is the population after 5 years? (nearest whole number)

misconceptions.message: 68 000 takes off 15% in one go (3% × 5). Compound: 80 000 × 0.97⁵ = 68 699.
72 000 is only 80 000 × 0.9, too big a single cut. Use 0.97 five times: 68 699.

bronze.hint: A quarter of £60. Split £60 into four equal parts.

misconceptions.message: £12 is 20% of £60 (dividing by 5). 25% is a quarter, so £60 ÷ 4 = £15.
£25 just copies the 25 from 25%. It means a quarter of £60, which is £15.
3.4 is 1% of 340 (dividing by 100). For 10%, divide by 10: 340 ÷ 10 = 34.
340 is the whole amount unchanged. 10% means one tenth: 340 ÷ 10 = 34.

bronze.hint: Find 15% of £200, then add it on. Or multiply by 1.15.

misconceptions.message: £30 is 15% of £200, the increase on its own. Add it back: 200 + 30 = £230.
£170 has 15% taken off. The question says increase, so add: £230.

bronze.hint: Find 20% of 80, then subtract. Or multiply by 0.8.

misconceptions.message: 16 is 20% of 80, the amount removed. Take it off: 80 − 16 = 64.
96 adds 20% instead. Decrease means subtract: 80 − 16 = 64.
60 takes off a flat 20. 20% of 80 is 16, so 80 − 16 = 64.

bronze.hint: Reduced by 10% means multiply by 0.9 (or take 10% off).
bronze.display: A shirt costs \(\pounds 35\). It is reduced by 10%. What is the sale price?

misconceptions.message: £38.50 adds 10%. Reduced means subtract: 35 − 3.50 = £31.50.
£3.50 is the 10% discount, not the price. Take it off £35: £31.50.
£25 takes off a flat £10. 10% of £35 is £3.50, so £31.50.

bronze.hint: Multiply a decimal by 100 to make it a percentage.

misconceptions.message: 3.5% only multiplies by 10. A decimal becomes a percentage by ×100: 0.35 × 100 = 35%.
0.35% just adds a % sign. Multiply by 100 first: 0.35 × 100 = 35%.
350% multiplies by 1000. It is only ×100: 35%.

bronze.hint: Divide the part by the whole, then multiply by 100.

misconceptions.message: 18% just copies the 18. Divide part by whole: 18 ÷ 60 = 0.3 = 30%.
42 is 60 − 18, the part left over. The question wants 18 as a percentage: 30%.
40 just repeats the 40 from 40%. 40% of 250 is 0.4 × 250 = 100.
150 is 60% of 250, what is left after 40%. The question wants 40%: 100.

silver.hint: Simple interest: find one year, then multiply by 3.
silver.display: \(\pounds 8000\) is invested at 5% simple interest for 3 years. What is the total interest earned?

misconceptions.message: £400 is one year's interest. Simple interest repeats it: 400 × 3 = £1200.
£1261 is the compound interest. This is simple interest: 8000 × 0.05 × 3 = £1200.
£9200 is the final balance (8000 + 1200). The question asks for the interest: £1200.

silver.hint: Find 2% of 50 000, then add it on.
silver.display: A population of 50 000 grows by 2% per year. What is the population after 1 year?

misconceptions.message: 50 200 adds only 200. 2% of 50 000 is 1000, so the total is 51 000.

silver.hint: Multiply by 0.9 each year, so use 0.9 squared.
silver.display: A car worth \(\pounds 16\,000\) depreciates by 10% per year. What is it worth after 2 years?

misconceptions.message: £12 800 takes 20% off in one go. Depreciation compounds: 16000 × 0.9² = £12 960.
£14 400 is after 1 year. Apply 0.9 again for year 2: 14400 × 0.9 = £12 960.
45% just repeats the 45. Divide part by whole: 45 ÷ 180 = 0.25 = 25%.
4 comes from 180 ÷ 45, the wrong way round. It is 45 ÷ 180 = 25%.

silver.hint: Divide the profit by the ORIGINAL price, then ×100.
silver.display: A house was bought for \(\pounds 150\,000\) and sold for \(\pounds 180\,000\). What is the percentage profit?

misconceptions.message: 16.7% divides by the selling price. Percentage change uses the original: 30000 ÷ 150000 = 20%.
£30 000 is the cash profit, not a percentage. As a percentage of 150 000 it is 20%.

silver.display: \(\pounds 6000\) invested at 4% compound interest for 3 years. Find the final amount.

misconceptions.message: £6720 uses simple interest (6000 + 3 × 240). Compound needs 6000 × 1.04³ = £6749.18.
£6240 is after 1 year. Apply 1.04 three times: 6000 × 1.04³ = £6749.18.

silver.display: VAT at 20% is added to a bill of \(\pounds 85\). What is the total?

misconceptions.message: £17 is the VAT (20% of 85). Add it on: 85 + 17 = £102.
£68 takes the VAT off. VAT is added: 85 × 1.2 = £102.
